title: Rafael and the Trail
premise: Bush pilot Isandro Dravenmoor has spent a decade ferrying medicine and secrets into the interior, keeping his past sealed as tightly as the crates he hauls. When the river recedes and reveals a chest bearing the seal of Vessania—a drowned nation he once served—he realizes the wreck below holds proof of what really happened to his crew, and that the salvage fleet closing in will bury the truth along with the bodies. Racing six tides against Captain Maren Kolvek's dredgers, Isandro must decide whether loyalty to the found family who sheltered him matters more than the truth they never asked him for. In the end, he chooses truth: he surfaces the wreck, names the dead, and loses his invisibility but gains a family that stays anyway.
about_author: Coral Whitlock is a former river guide who writes adventure fiction from a houseboat on the northern coast, where she collects tide charts and other people's rumors. Her novels are known for wilderness settings that feel like characters and heroes who would rather disappear than be thanked.

chapters.title: The River Gives Back
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A routine medicine run ends when low water exposes a rusted chest stamped with Vessania's seal—the nation that officially never existed. He nearly leaves it, but pockets the seal plate instead. Emotional beat: dread disguised as curiosity; the past knocking before he's ready to answer.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the trading post, he learns the salvage fleet of Captain Maren Kolvek arrives in six tides, licensed to strip everything from the riverbed—including, he suspects, evidence. His old friend Odile begs him to fly out and stay invisible. Emotional beat: the first crack between loyalty to his quiet life and the pull of truth.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, flashback woven through present dive. He free-dives the wreck at night and finds the crew compartment of the Vessanian transport—his old crew's tags still inside. Flashback: the mission he was ordered to abandon. Emotional beat: grief surfacing with the wreckage; guilt made physical.

chapters.title: The Family That Took Him In
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The trading-post community—Odile, mechanic Tam, young runner Pip—debate whether Isandro has been lying to them for ten years or protecting them. Pip defends him fiercely. Emotional beat: belonging tested by suspicion; found family under strain without breaking.

chapters.title: Kolvek Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The fleet shows up two tides ahead of schedule; Kolvek recognizes Isandro from the old service and offers him a cut to point her at the crew compartment—or else she'll dig up everything, including his name. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve; the trap of complicity.

chapters.title: Tam's Hands
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam discovers Isandro's hidden flight logs and confronts him privately. Instead of betrayal, Tam offers to rig the fleet's dredge pumps to fail—if Isandro tells the others the truth himself first. Emotional beat: grace offered on hard terms; accountability over absolution.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. On the exposed mudflats, Isandro tells Odile, Tam, and Pip everything: the sealed orders, the abandoned crew, why he ran. Pip takes his hand; Odile walks away angry but doesn't leave. Emotional beat: the cost of truth paid openly; loyalty redefined rather than lost.

chapters.title: Sabotage and Storm
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Isandro and Tam. The sabotage works until a storm surge lets the fleet work through the night; Kolvek's divers reach the crew compartment. Isandro flies into the storm to drop flares and force a halt, nearly losing the plane. Emotional beat: rising action cresting—sacrifice as proof of changed loyalties.

chapters.title: The Wreck Belongs to the Dead
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Climax: Isandro lands on Kolvek's barge and invokes an obscure salvage law—wrecks carrying human remains belong to their nation of registry—and produces the seal plate, forcing the fleet to stand down pending review. Kolvek, grudgingly respectful, withdraws. Emotional beat: triumph earned not by force but by finally standing visible and accountable.

chapters.title: Names on the Water
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Weeks later, the community raises a marker on the mudflat bearing the crew's recovered names. Odile returns; Pip paints the plane's tail with the Vessian seal. Isandro stays—not hidden anymore, just home. Emotional beat: resolution; truth didn't cost him his family, it made one worth having.
